newsitem.title: USA: Spalding Cty, Ga., rejects merger, oks school tax.
newsitem.headline: Spalding Cty, Ga., rejects merger, oks school tax.

text.p: Voters rejected a proposal to merge Georgia's Spalding County and City of Griffin governments, but approved a countywide sales tax increase for schools, city officials said Wednesday.
The consolidation measure was defeated by several thousand votes, although exact totals were unavailable.
If it had passed, the county would have assumed Griffin's bond indebtedness, including $128 million in bond responsibility to the Municipal Electric Authority Group.
Separately, Spalding County voters approved a one-cent sales tax increase for schools. It passed with 57 percent of the votes.

The Spalding school district was one of 69 Georgia school districts voting Tuesday on the local option sales tax for schools. A constitutional amendment approved by voters in November allowed districts to levy the one-cent tax increase for up to five years to fund school construction and retire outstanding debt.
The school tax will be used to pay debt service on $41 million of school construction bonds that voters approved in September.
The bonds were issued with the provision that if the sales tax proposal failed, property tax rates would rise by 11 percent for 19 years to pay debt service on the bonds.
